subject: Temporary threshold increase & surge terms — short window proposal
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@acmeai.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — short surge window and billing for Oct 31

Hi Lauren,

We ran a surprise spike in model usage yesterday tied to a marketing push and will likely exceed our monthly quota for a 36-hour window around Oct 31. Can Redwood temporarily raise our request threshold by ~3x for that window?

Two asks: 1) Can you confirm the rate-limit bump and the maximum sustained TPS we can get on our Dedicated pool? 2) How will overage billing work — are you able to provide a short-term credit or pro-rated charge rather than full overrun rates?

I attached a small spreadsheet with our expected token profile for the surge (quota-request.xlsx). If you can outline options (burst only, burst+grace credit, or commit uplift) we can decide quickly.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Tom
Director of Infrastructure
Acme AI

Attachment: quota-request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acmeai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short surge window and billing for Oct 31

Hi Tom — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Short answer: yes, we can provision a temporary headroom window but we need to align on the commercial guardrails.

Options I propose (fast path):
- Burst-only: temporary rate-limit lift for the 36-hour window, billed at overrun unit rates (standard overrun rate). No credits.
- Burst + grace credit: same lift, plus a one-time credit that offsets up to 30% of the incremental overrun charge (applied on the invoice following the surge).
- Short commit: convert expected surge tokens into a 1-month committed uplift at a discounted unit rate (requires a brief amendment).

Can you confirm the expected token volume and whether Acme prefers an invoice credit vs. a committed uplift? If you want the grace credit path we can draft a short amendment to the contract (proposed-amendment.docx).

I'll loop in Aditya on approval/discounts and Marcus on capacity planning — Marcus, can our Dedicated pool sustain a 3x sustained TPS for Oct 31–Nov 1 without impacting other tenants?

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: proposed-amendment.docx (draft amendment)

Date: 2026-10-25T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short surge window and billing for Oct 31

Lauren — we can absorb a 3x sustained TPS from Acme for a 36-hour window if we reserve an isolated burst pool and schedule spillover controls. Two operational notes:
1) We'll put them on a temporary headroom pool pinned to their Dedicated nodes to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
2) We should cap the absolute token rate per-second and set an automated fallback to their compatible hosted variant if the Dedicated pool saturates.

This will cost us some pre-reserved capacity for the 36-hour window (minimal), and we should gate it behind an approved commercial patch.

Aditya — what's our recommended credit level for a short, one-time surge? Suggest 20–35% credit depending on strategic importance. For a quick close I can support 25% credit applied to overrun tokens up to the volume in Tom's spreadsheet.

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-26T09:08:00-07:00

Thanks team — I reviewed Acme's usage history and strategic fit. Recommendation: approve a 25% one-time credit on incremental overrun for this event, with the following guardrails:
- Credit caps at the token volume in quota-request.xlsx.
- Customer signs a 1-month amendment that documents the burst window and billing treatment (we'll use proposed-amendment.docx with a short-term annex).
- We require a 48-hour lead to configure the pinned burst pool; if they request <48 hours we apply a 10% administrative surcharge on top of the overrun rate.

Lauren — if you get Tom's confirmation I can issue the commercial approval and finance will note the credit on the next invoice. Marcus — engineering readiness accepted.

Aditya Rao
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
